Kai (prod): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands sec segment. Customers wanted a single-paragraph FAQ: what BYOQ vs BYOK means, how audit exports prove integrity for SOC2/ISO, and expected Private/VPC logging behavior. Can security/compliance distill this?

Jordan (security): Short FAQ draft: BYOK = you manage keys in a cloud KMS we integrate with (we never see plaintext). BYOQ = key material stays in your HSM; Redwood records an HSM attestation blob included in audit bundles. For integrity: daily signed bundles contain events.ndjson.gz, a manifest with SHA256 checksums, and a detached signature; auditors can verify checksums and signature to prove exports weren't tampered with.

Tara (compliance): Addendum for auditors: we can include rotation logs and a signed export receipt with timestamp on request. Recommended customer-facing sentence: "Default log retention is 90 days; customers can enable daily signed exports to their storage for long-term retention and audit evidence."

Ilya (infra): Tech notes: exports are gzipped and named like exports/YYYY-MM-DD/<tenant>/audit-bundle-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz. Full payload capture is opt-in and truncated by default (8KB) to avoid accidental PII retention; enabling full logs surfaces estimated egress/storage costs in the console.

Kai (prod): Perfect. Can someone put the one-paragraph FAQ and an example filename in the sales enablement doc and link it in here?

Support Bot: Reminder: Security office hours "Audit exports & KMS" on 2010003600 — RSVP: https://calendar.redwood.company/officehours-security :bell:

Jordan (security): Action items: I'll post the verification commands + public key, Tara will draft the auditor checklist by Friday, Ilya will add filename and lifecycle examples to docs. Kai will add the one-paragraph to sales enablement.

Tara (compliance): Thanks all — ping me directly for customer-specific retention >1 year or HSM attestation requests. :white_check_mark:
